key_insight: Hot-wire plasma arc WAAM can deposit titanium with optimized parameters and effective inert shielding, producing low-contamination builds with controllable properties.
engineering_relevance: The study supports a scalable route to lower-cost titanium part fabrication for aerospace and other high-performance applications.
method: Used a specialized inert gas shielding device to prevent titanium oxidation during melting.
Applied full-factorial DOE in Minitab to optimize welding speed, wire current, and wire feed rate.
Evaluated deposits using EDS, 3D microscopy, and mechanical testing.
evidence_signal: EDS reported zero oxygen contamination, while mechanical tests showed UTS of 560.80–693.58 MPa horizontally and 631.65–677.10 MPa vertically, with hardness ranging from 199.8 to 266.8 HV.
watch_item: The build shows anisotropic strength and hardness variation across height, so parameter transfer and part qualification may require direction-specific validation.
paper_title: The process study and parameter influence in Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing (WAAM) of titanium using hot-wire plasma arc welding
